page: Google Cloud Platform e2-medium is a shared-core virtual machine instance within the E2 family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and utilizes an Intel Xeon processor operating at a base frequency of 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs, which are mapped to a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled, representing a fractional shared physical core allocation. It includes 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor cache configuration consists of 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include any bundled local storage or GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks reflect the shared-resource nature of the e2-medium instance. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is rated as average at 2642.19, whereas multi-core performance drops to the bottom 25% with a score of 2642.78 due to shared-core resource limits. Memory bandwidth is highly constrained, with large block read-only speeds at 6.36 GB/sec and write speeds at 4.83 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 10%. Geekbench scores also place the instance in the bottom 10%, showing a single-core score of 661.0 and a multi-core score of 682.0. Redis SET operations achieve 0.82 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is limited to 0.63 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-medium offers an economical entry point for hosting workloads that do not require sustained, high-performance CPU or memory resources. The shared-core architecture allows for resource density and lower operational costs, though it introduces performance tradeoffs during periods of high resource contention. This instance is appropriate for low-traffic web servers, small microservices, development and testing environments, basic automation scripts, and lightweight background tasks that can tolerate variable CPU availability.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-medium is an entry-level, shared-core instance within the E2 family, designed for lightweight and cost-conscious workloads. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to a single physical Intel Xeon core at 2.2 GHz, with 4.0 GB of RAM and no bundled local storage or GPUs. Performance benchmarks reflect its shared-resource nature, with stress-ng single-core performance in the middle 50% range, while multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics fall into the lower percentiles. Specifically, large-block memory read bandwidth is limited to 6.36 GB/sec, and Geekbench multi-core scores average 682.0. This instance provides a highly cost-efficient profile for non-demanding applications. It is appropriate for development environments, low-traffic web serving, microservices, and basic background automation tasks where sustained high performance is not required.
